text:
Priya Patel: Heads up, since ~1801299000 we're seeing a surge of errors from the embeddings endpoint. Lots of 5xxs and customers reporting empty vectors. Main error group: "EmbeddingDimensionMismatch: expected 1536, incoming 768" and intermittent "batcher queue full" logs. Example request_id: req_e24b9f. Regions affected: eu-central, us-west-2.

incident-bot: [ALERT] embeddings 5xx rate increased from 0.8% -> 12.7%. Sentry: https://sentry.redwood/issue/embeddings/5591. Runbook: https://wiki.redwood/runbooks/embeddings.

Marco Ruiz: Oncall taking. Any deploys or catalog edits in the last 4h?

Jun Kim: I updated model alias mapping earlier to add new artifact `rwd-embed-large-1536` and bumped default_batch_token_limit from 6k -> 12k to improve throughput. No rolling restart yet.

Priya Patel: Repro attached (curl):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/embeddings -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"rwd-embed-large-1536","input":["hello world"]}'
```
Response:
{"error":"EmbeddingDimensionMismatch: expected 1536 got 768","request_id":"req_e24b9f"}

Alice Chen: Checking router -> I see some upstream workers advertising `model_dim=768` in /health and being returned by the shard allocator for the alias `rwd-embed-large-1536`. Catalog shows alias -> artifact 1536, but a subset of nodes still has older mount.

Marco Ruiz: So we have mixed-version pool. Could we have a race in the catalog distribution or stale mounts after the artifact update?

Jun Kim: Likely. The catalog service pushed alias change, but worker mount-sync is async; there's a window where an alias resolves to nodes that haven't switched artifacts. Also the batch token increase likely caused larger batch sizes, so when retries happen, batcher queue fills and you see "batcher queue full" causing 502s.

Priya Patel: Impact: several customers retry loops triggered, doubling token counts and increasing load. Support tickets from customers: cust-A12, cust-B33, cust-C88.

Kareem Singh: billing-bot flagged anomalous usage for those customers. Need a list of request_ids in window 1801296000-1801302000 to reconcile billing.

Alice Chen: Mitigations proposed:
- A: Add a router-level strict_model_check to reject routing to nodes with mismatched model_dim (fast).
- B: Temporarily rollback alias mapping to previous artifact until all nodes mount (safe but might reduce perf).
- C: Drain and cordon nodes that report mismatched metadata (manual ops).
- D: Reduce gateway retries and increase exponential backoff to avoid retry storms.

Marco Ruiz: Prioritize A + D immediately. B and C as follow-ups.

Jun Kim: I'll prepare a tiny router patch to enforce strict_model_check and return a clear 409/400 with tag `model_dim_mismatch`. Pushing PR now: https://git.redwood/runtime/pull/489. Also toggling alias rollback as option if needed.

ops-bot: Applying temporary gateway throttle: max_retries set to 1, initial_backoff 3s -> 8s.

Alice Chen: I started cordoning 4 nodes in eu-central that report 768; draining those from matching pools. Monitoring error rate.

Priya Patel: After cordon+gateway throttle, eu-central 5xx down from 13% -> 2.2% in 6 minutes. us-west-2 still at ~7.4%.

Jun Kim: Router hotfix deployed to canary; strict_model_check enabled. Router now rejects mismatched routing with 400 and label `model_dim_mismatch`. Telemetry events emitted for each reject.

Marco Ruiz: Good. That should prevent backend workers from throwing 500s and stop retry amplification.

Alice Chen: Continuing to drain mismatched nodes in us-west-2. Found that an automated prefetcher remounted old artifact on those machines during a failed migration attempt. Kicking the prefetcher job to force remount.

Priya Patel: Support: collecting all affected request IDs and writing to secure ticket for billing team. Also sending initial comms to customers that might be impacted.

Kareem Singh: Billing team to run reconciliation and apply credits to impacted accounts. I'll need the exported request list.

Jun Kim: Root cause hypothesis: race between catalog alias update and asynchronous worker artifact mount leading to mixed-dim pool; increased batch token limit aggravated retry/batcher overload when mismatches triggered retries.

Marco Ruiz: Action items:
- [P0] router strict_model_check (deployed)
- [P1] ensure synchronous alias -> all-nodes handshake in catalog propagation (Jun)
- [P1] fix prefetcher logic to avoid remounting old artifacts mid-rollout (Alice)
- [P2] add auto-suppression of retries after 5xx burst at gateway (Marco)
- [P2] billing reconciliation and customer comms (Kareem/Priya)

Alice Chen: Confirmed all nodes now advertise model_dim=1536 for `rwd-embed-large-1536`. Drains complete.

Priya Patel: Post-mit metrics: global 5xx at 0.4%, 4xx increased due to router rejects (expected). Customers are getting vectors again. Preparing postmortem draft and internal timeline.

Kareem Singh: Billing credits queued and initial customer messages drafted. Will finalize after postmortem.

incident-bot: Incident resolved. Incident ID: INC-2026-03-15-23.

Marco Ruiz: Thanks all. I'll close oncall slate after postmortem. Reopen if regression.

Priya Patel: Great response everyone. I'll post the postmortem link when ready. :thumbsup:
